name: base64-simd
baseline: the base64 crate's scalar engine (version not stated in the dashboard)
verdict_reason: Its 2023 dashboard showed 6.0x faster encoding and 8.5x faster decoding than the base64 crate on large inputs. base64 0.23 (2026-07) added its own AVX2/NEON engine measured at 3.8x encode and 7.1x decode over its scalar path, so most of that gap is gone for callers who opt in. No head-to-head has been published since, and base64-simd has had no release since 0.8.0 (2022-12).
tier_reason: First-party dashboard generated by CI; benchmark code is public but the CPU and toolchain are not stated.
claimed_speedup: decode 11.010 vs 1.289 GiB/s at 87384 bytes (8.5x), 1.097 vs 0.524 GiB/s at 24 bytes (2.1x); encode 9.216 vs 1.538 GiB/s at 65536 bytes (6.0x), 1.347 vs 0.491 GiB/s at 16 bytes (2.7x) (ratios derived from page data)
workload: Encode and decode of byte buffers from 16 bytes to 87 KB, runtime-detected SIMD ('dynamic' section) vs base64's scalar engine.
platforms: runtime dispatch among AVX2, SSSE3/SSE2, NEON and wasm simd128 kernels; scalar fallback
one_liner: SIMD base64 encoder/decoder; 6x-8.5x faster than the base64 crate in 2023, a gap base64 0.23's own SIMD engine has mostly closed.
how_it_is_fast: Uses the vectorized base64 algorithms of Wojciech Muła and aqrit cited in the README, compiled for AVX2, SSSE3, NEON and wasm simd128 and chosen at runtime, with a scalar fallback.
use_it_when: Projects pinned to base64 0.22 or older that need SIMD now
Forgiving (whitespace-tolerant) decoding at SIMD speed, which base64-simd offers and the dashboard measured
skip_it_when: You can use base64 0.23+ and construct its Simd engine
You want an actively released crate: the last base64-simd release is 0.8.0 from 2022-12-28
caveats: First-party numbers from 2023-04 with no hardware stated
The base64 version compared is not named; it predates base64's SIMD engine
The dashboard issue was closed and moved to Nugine/simd-benches, which publishes no text results
tradeoffs: The README says the project relies heavily on unsafe code

evidence.quote: This project relies heavily on unsafe code.
